slides.title: Use the official TAL lease.

photo.credit: Église Saint-Vincent-de-Paul, Laval · Photo: Jeangagnon, CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons

slides.body: From Saint-Vincent-de-Paul to Pont-Viau, every new residential lease must use the TAL form. Mandatory since **1996**.
slides.source: Per Tribunal administratif du logement, Nov 2026

slides.title: No security deposit at signing.
slides.body: Québec's Civil Code bars any payment other than rent. A deposit is legal only if the tenant freely offers it.

slides.title: Raising rent? Mind the calendar.
slides.body: For a lease of **12 months or more**. A tenant who says nothing within a month has accepted.

slides.title: If the tenant says no.

banner.text: 1 month to apply to the TAL

slides.body: Miss that window and the lease renews at the **same rent**. The TAL's calculation method changed on Jan. 1, 2026.

slides.title: Price the leases, not just the plex.
slides.body: Current rents and lease terms come with the building. Read every lease with your notary before you offer.
